studies.Population: Adults aged 30–79 years with histologically confirmed urinary bladder carcinoma and frequency-matched controls from Maine, Vermont, and New Hampshire
studies.Smoking Status: Never, occasional, former, and current smokers included and adjusted for
studies.Ethnicity Basis: Default: no protocol-mapped specific country or population was established
studies.Ethnicity Supporting Text: The majority of the study subjects were White (94.5% and 94.7% for cases and controls, respectively).
studies.Reference: Dietary intake of meat, fruits, vegetables, and selective micronutrients and risk of bladder cancer in the New England region of the United States.
studies.Authors: Wu JW, Cross AJ, Baris D, Ward MH, Karagas MR, Johnson A, Schwenn M, Cherala S, Colt JS, Cantor KP, Rothman N, Silverman DT, Sinha R
studies.Timing: Dietary intake during the previous 5 years
studies.comparison_type: Highest versus lowest quartile of dietary vitamin B12 intake

sample_size.excerpt: A total of 1068 cases (811 men and 257 women) and 1266 controls (927 men and 339 women) were included in our analysis ( Table 1 ).
sample_size.location: Results; Table 1; total_n derived from reported group counts 1068 + 1266 = 2334

cases.excerpt: A total of 1068 cases (811 men and 257 women) and 1266 controls (927 men and 339 women) were included in our analysis ( Table 1 ).

effect_size.excerpt: We did, however, observe an inverse association with vitamin B12 intake (OR: 0.77; 95% CI: 0.61-0.99; P=0.019).

confidence_interval.excerpt: We did, however, observe an inverse association with vitamin B12 intake (OR: 0.77; 95% CI: 0.61-0.99; P=0.019).

p_value.excerpt: We did, however, observe an inverse association with vitamin B12 intake (OR: 0.77; 95% CI: 0.61-0.99; P=0.019).

comparison.excerpt: Individuals in the highest, compared with the lowest, quartile of vitamin B12 intake had a lower risk of bladder cancer (OR: 0.77; 95% CI: 0.61–0.99; P =0.019).
comparison.location: Results; Vitamins from diet and risk of bladder cancer, Table 6

design.excerpt: We conducted a population-based case–control study of bladder cancer in Maine, New Hampshire, and Vermont.

continent.excerpt: The cases and controls were mostly from Maine and New Hampshire.

ethnicity.excerpt: The majority of the study subjects were White (94.5% and 94.7% for cases and controls, respectively).
